newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Ferrell FX Index up 1.3 pct in September.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Ferrell FX Index up 1.3 pct in September.

text.p: The Ferrell FX Index rose 1.3 percent in September with the median return up 0.5 percent, Ferrell Capital Management said on Monday.
Twenty-five of 36 programs reported positive results in September, Ferrell said.
Friedberg Commodity Management Inc, of Toronto, turned in the month's top performance, reporting gains of 9.3 percent.

"We switched our long exposure in the deutschemarks and the Swiss francs into a long British pound position," Friedberg vice president Rick Zauderer told Ferrell. "Our performance of 9.3 percent this month was enhanced by the decline of the Japanese yen, which we are short, and the continued appreciation of the New Zealand dollar long position," he said.
New York City-based Tamiso & Co placed second in the survey, showing a rise of 8.0 percent, and MicroQuant Capital Management Corp of Greenwich, Conn., placed third with gains of 5.9 percent.
"The full year 1996 has been a sideways movement with wide swings within ranges," said S. Waite Rawls of Ferrell Capital Management.
For the 117-month period from January 1987 through September 1996, the compounded annual return of the Ferrell FX index is 17.4 percent.

The index provides a benchmark for multi-advisor currency portfolios and includes 36 programs managed by 33 firms located in the United States, United Kingdom, France, Canada, Ireland and Switzerland.
